full_judgment:
8. In the case of Mazulla Vs. The State reported in PLD 1961 (Pesh) 7 the question relating to making attempt for penetration was raised and the accused was convicted by the trial Court under section 377/511 of the Penal Code on the Charge of making attempt to commit sodomy. On appeal the conviction was altered and reduced to sections 342/ 323 of the Penal Code on the grounds and with the findings that the accused could not be said to have committed the offence under sections 377/511 as the prosecution could not prove that there was an attempt of penetration by the accused. In the present case the burden lies more heavily on the prosecution to prove the act of penetration as there is specific allegation of having carnal intercourse by way of penetration of the penis of the accused in the anus of the victim and it is to be seen as to how far the prosecution has been able to discharge the said burden. 

 12. Let us now see who are the witnesses in the case and how far they have proved the charge of the commission of unnatural offence by the accused petitioner. Out of 8 witnesses cited in the charge-sheet only 3 witnesses have been examined. The age of the victim P.W. 1 has not been disclosed anywhere in the ease. The age of the victim may not be material to constitute an offence of sodomy but it is no doubt a factor for ascertaining the gravity of the offence and the assessing the value of the evidence of the witnesses. In his deposition P.W. 1 introduced for the first time a new story saying that he was taken in a room and the accused-petitioner satisfied his carnal lust by penetrating his penis in his anus. This version of the P.W. 1, on the face of it, appears to be a departure from and improvement by way of addition to his earlier version given in the First Information Report which contains only such statement that the accused opened the lungi of P.W. 1 and eased indecent foul act (খারাপ কাজ) on him. P.W. 1 appears to have become wiser as days passed and introduced the word penetration during evidence so as to make out a case of unnatural offence when he came to understand that me statement similar to those made in the F.I.R. may not be found to be sufficient to constitute an offence under section 377 of the Penal Code. Out of the 3 witness examined, P.W. 1 Yunus Ali is the informant who is said to be the victim. P.W. 2 Yasin is the brother of P.W. 1 and P.W. 3 Ansar is the only independent witness in the case. It is to be seen who are the witnesses and how far they have proved the charge of sodomy against the accused petitioner. P.W. 1 is the witness giving out the prosecution case and entire case rests on his sole testimony. P.W. 2 Yasin Ali is the elder brother of P.W. 1 and is said to head heard about the incident from the victim. This witness added that the victim was examined by a doctor but unfortunately no medical report is available in the case. There is no other evidence of independent witness to corroborate the evidence of P.W. 1. True it is that such a disgraceful act of perpetration of sodomy is not done in presence of others and hence the prosecution is not expected to produce eye witness regarding the commission of the offence, But the prosecution is not absolved of the burden to produce such arterials or evidence which may lend support to the evidence of P.W. 1 leading to the inference that he was so demised by the accused petitioner, Thus the evidence of P.W. l that he went to the house of the accused-petitioner to fetch medicine, that he came back home crying or that there was any mark of assault on the anus of P.W. 1 have remained uncorroborated. Moreover, the prosecution. has failed to produce any medical report or doctor to prove the charge of the commission of unnatural offence to ascertain the condition of the person on whom act of sodomy was said to have been perpetrated or, at any rate, to get some proof-as to the condition of the anus of the victim immediately after the alleged act of unnatural intercourse. Medical report is very vital and the absence of the medical report in the case casts a serious doubt on the prosecution case, P.W.3 is the only independent witness examined in the case and be has also belied the prosecution case as he flatly denied to have any knowledge about the occurrence. 

 13. Mr. Akram Hossain Amin, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the prosecution has miserably failed to prove the charge of sodomy by any tangible evidence but the learned courts below without sifting, weighing and considering the evidence on record in its true perspective have arrived at an erroneous decision which has occasioned a failure of justice. In the present case since charge is of committing unnatural offence by way of penetration of male organ of the accused in the anus of the complainant the burden heavily lies on the prosecution to prove the alleged act by reliable and convincing evidence. From the evidence on record it reveals that P.W. I did not say about his being examined by any doctor but P.W, 2 stated that the victim was examined by a doctor but no medical certificate was issued. Non-examination of the victim by any doctor or in the alternative, if the victim was at all examined, non submission of medical report and absence of medical evidence has rendered the prosecution case highly doubtful. In this respect the learned advocate for the petitioner referred the case of Mirro Vs. Emperor reported in A.I.R. 1947 All 97 and the case of Emperor Vs. Sami Des reported. in A.I.R. 1926 Lah 375. In both the cases their Lordships disbelieved the prosecution case and acquitted the accused. In the First mentioned case the Medical report did not support the prosecution allegation of sodomy and in the second mentioned case there was no medical evidence to show that the complainant was subjected to unnatural offence. In the instant case also neither the medical report nor medical evidence is available to support the allegation of P.W, 1 and hence no reliance can be placed on the uncorroborated sole testimony of the victim in the absence of any medico legal evidence. 

 14. Next, the learned advocate Mr. Akram Hossain Amin has taken us through the judgment of the courts below and submits that the trial court as well as the court of appeal below having failed to apply their judicial mind in arriving at the finding of guilt against the accused petitioner the judgment and order of conviction have occasioned a failure of justice and hence cannot be sustained. On perusal of the judgments of the courts below it is found that the learned trial court convicted the accused petitioner against the weight of evidence throwing the burden of proof entirely on the defence holding that the talk of amicable settlement between the parties became corroborative proof of alleged occurrence in total ignorance of the established principle of Criminal jurisprudence. The learned appellate court also has not arrived at any independent finding of its own after due consideration of the evidence, rather fully depended on the finding of the trial court and thus the appellate court also committed error of law in affirming the judgment of the trial court. Though ordinarily the High Court does not interfere with the concurrent finding of facts arrived at by the courts below, but the instant case is an exception as the trial court as well as the appellate court have completely overlooked some striking features and glaring defects appearing on the face of the prosecution case which have vitiated the findings of fact. Such a wrong approach, therefore, by both the courts below has resulted in a serious miscarriage of justice calling for interference in this revision case.
